situation.text: Hoje você conhece Aaron, de Salt Lake City. Receita simples e ingredientes.

pages.goal: Hoje você aprende a contar os passos de uma receita com first, then, next e finally, cozinhando com a mãe.

pages.hook: In many American homes, the kitchen is the center of the house. Friends talk, kids help, and everyone ends up standing near the stove.
pages.polite: When you help in someone else's kitchen, ask first: **“Can I help?”** Then listen to the steps.

mythfact.s: American recipes often use cups and tablespoons.
mythfact.why: Many US recipes measure by volume: a cup of flour, a tablespoon of oil.
Ovens in the USA use degrees Fahrenheit, for example 350°F.

mythfact.s: A guest can ask “Can I help?” in the kitchen.
mythfact.why: It is friendly and normal, and hosts often say yes.

mythfact.s: You should touch a pan to see if it is hot.
mythfact.why: Never touch it. Say “Careful! The pan is hot!” and use a pot holder.

compare.tip: When you read an American recipe, check the unit first: cup, tablespoon or degrees F.

pages.title: Reading quest — Pasta night with my roommate
text: On Sunday night, my roommate Aaron and I cooked together in our small kitchen. He opened the fridge and asked, “**What are you making?**” I smiled and said, “**Pasta with tomato sauce**.”

Aaron wanted to help. “**Can I help?**” he asked. “**Sure**,” I said. “**Cut the onions, please**.” He took a knife and a cutting board. “**How many?**” he asked. “**Just one**,” I said. “Then **add the tomatoes**.”
I put a big pan on the stove and added some oil and a little salt. The kitchen smelled so good! Aaron came near the stove, and I said, “**Careful! The pan is hot**.” He stepped back and laughed.

My family always says that cooking is like a game. First you cut, then you fry, next you add, and finally you taste. In my country we cook rice and beans, but tonight we made pasta, and it was a lot of fun.

When the sauce was ready, I put the pasta on two plates. Aaron looked at his plate and said, “**Dinner is served!**” We sat at the small table and ate slowly. The food was simple, but it was delicious.
